Optional in whole and in part — every field may be omitted, and omitting the part entirely reproduces the review exactly as it ran before declarations existed. Values are validated against the schema `/api/config` publishes.

file.description: The permit set, as a PDF.

file.title: File

declaration_fields.description: The whole questionnaire, as data. Adding a field or an enum value in `fbcreview/declaration_schema.py` reaches the client through here with no frontend change.
declaration_fields.title: Declaration Fields

declaration_groups.description: Question groups, in the order the form should show them.
declaration_groups.title: Declaration Groups

declaration_unlockable.description: Every rule any declaration field unlocks, deduplicated.
declaration_unlockable.title: Declaration Unlockable

rules.description: Rule ids registered in this build.

severities.description: Severity floor choices, most severe first.

ConversionReport.description:
What the raster rebuild actually recovered.

Reported rather than summarised away: if OCR found 40 characters on a
sheet, the review that follows is thin and the person needs to know why.

traced_layer.description: Optional-content group the traced linework is written to. Deliberately not named after any semantic CAD layer — tracing recovers lines, not what they mean.
traced_layer.title: Traced Layer

ConversionReport.title: ConversionReport

DeclarationField.description:
One question, in both vocabularies.

The client renders whatever this describes and must not carry a copy of any
label, help text or enum value: a code label that exists in two places will
drift, and a wrong code label is a liability rather than a typo.

unlocks.description: Rule ids this answer enables. The client divides by these to say how many checks will stand down without it.
unlocks.title: Unlocks

DeclarationField.title: DeclarationField

DeclarationReport.description: What was submitted and what the drawings said back. The audit trail.
DeclarationReport.title: DeclarationReport

DeclarationTolerance.description:
How far apart two numbers may be before they count as disagreeing.

Effective tolerance is `max(abs, rel * value)`. Rounding on a drawing is not
a conflict; a different governing row is.
DeclarationTolerance.title: DeclarationTolerance

Downloads.description: V4 signed URLs, fetched straight from Cloud Storage by the browser.
Downloads.title: Downloads

available.description: False editions are listed and disabled, not hidden.
available.title: Available

message.description: Prose safe to show a person.
message.title: Message

ErrorResponse.description: The only shape any failure takes.
ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse

basis.description: What the finding rests on. `declaration` means the drawings do not state the value it depends on, and the card says so — the markup must never attribute to the drawings something the drawings do not say.
basis.title: Basis

scenario.description: Which reading produced this. `both` means it came out the same whether the set was evaluated as drawn or as declared, which is the common case. `as_drawn` means it appeared only against the drawings; `as_declared` only against the declaration.
scenario.title: Scenario

FindingsDocument.description:
The exact shape of `findings.json` in the bucket.

No endpoint serves this — the browser fetches it from the signed URL — but
it is published into `components.schemas` (see `server.custom_openapi`) so
the generated TypeScript client carries the type. Without that the findings
table would be the one part of the client typed by hand, which is precisely
the part most likely to drift.

declaration.description: Present when a project declaration was submitted.

FindingsDocument.title: FindingsDocument

Health.description:
Deliberately cheap: no Firestore or Cloud Storage call. Cloud Run's
startup probe hits this.

auth_required.description: Whether this deployment demands a Firebase ID token. False only on a deliberately open build. The client reads it here rather than inferring it, because guessing wrong in either direction is bad: guess `true` on an open deployment and the tool is unreachable; guess `false` on a real one and every request 401s behind a UI that claims you are signed in.
auth_required.title: Auth Required

Health.title: Health

HistoryEntry.description:
One past review, as the history list shows it.

Deliberately not the whole `Job`. A list of thirty rows does not need thirty
sets of signed download URLs, and minting them costs a round trip each —
the client asks for `GET /api/jobs/{id}` when a row is actually opened.

counts.description: Findings by severity, from the stored summary. Empty until done.
counts.title: Counts

declared_fields.description: How many declaration questions were answered.
declared_fields.title: Declared Fields

HistoryEntry.title: HistoryEntry

HistoryResponse.description: The caller's own reviews, newest first. Never anyone else's.
HistoryResponse.title: HistoryResponse

conversion.description: Present when scanned sheets were rebuilt.

declaration.description: What was submitted with the review, if anything.

filename.description: Basename as uploaded. Never a path.
filename.title: Filename

source.description: What kind of PDF was uploaded, measured at admission.

id.description: Value submitted with a review, e.g. `A-3`.
id.title: Id

PrefillResponse.description: What a set states about itself, read without starting a review.

fields.description: Only fields the drawings actually state. A set whose code data block is a pasted picture yields very few, which is the honest answer for that set and exactly the case the declaration exists to cover.
fields.title: Fields

PrefillResponse.title: PrefillResponse

PrefilledField.description:
One declaration answer the drawings already state.

A suggestion, never a decision. The applicant confirms or overrides it, and
what they submit is what gets declared — the reconciliation is only worth
running if the two sides stay independent, and a silently auto-accepted
value would make every field agree with itself.

key.description: A declaration field key, as `/api/config` publishes it.
key.title: Key

source.description: Where on the set it was read, e.g. "G-0 project data".
source.title: Source

value.description: Rendered as the field's control holds it, never typed.
value.title: Value

PrefilledField.title: PrefilledField

ProjectDeclaration.description:
What the applicant says the building is, answered before uploading.

Every field is optional and `null` means unanswered. There is deliberately
no "unknown" sentinel: a rule that receives `null` abstains, and it can
never mistake a placeholder for an answer.

Mirrors `fbcreview.declaration.ProjectDeclaration`. Values are validated
against `fbcreview.declaration_schema` before a review starts, so an enum
value this build does not know is a 400 naming the field rather than a
silently dropped answer.
ProjectDeclaration.title: ProjectDeclaration

RasterRegion.description: A pasted image large enough to plausibly hold a table.
RasterRegion.title: RasterRegion

ReconciledField.description: One field, with what each source said about it and how they compare.

drawn_source.description: The sheet the drawn value was read from.
drawn_source.title: Drawn Source

ReconciledField.title: ReconciledField

convert_raster.description: Rebuild scanned sheets before reviewing: OCR to recover a text layer, and trace the linework into real vector paths. Off by default because it turns a two-second review into a multi-minute one. Recovers text, not meaning — traced lines carry no CAD layer names, so geometric rules still abstain.
convert_raster.title: Convert Raster

email_to.description: Inert unless SMTP is configured on the server. Not surfaced in the web client.
email_to.title: Email To

occupancy_group.description: Deprecated. Occupancy group is a fact about the building, not a review setting, and belongs in the project declaration. Sent explicitly, it seeds `declaration.occupancy_group` when the declaration does not state one; left at its default it is ignored and nothing is assumed.
occupancy_group.title: Occupancy Group

sprinklered.description: Deprecated, as `occupancy_group`. Sent explicitly it seeds `declaration.sprinkler_system` as an NFPA 13 system or none.
sprinklered.title: Sprinklered

SheetProfile.description:
Measured, not guessed: drawing-primitive count, live character count and
how much of the page is covered by raster images.
SheetProfile.title: SheetProfile

SourceProfile.description:
Whether this set is readable, and which sheets are not.

A scanned sheet produces no findings, and no findings reads as a clean
sheet. Publishing this lets the client say "not checked" where the truth is
"could not be read".

region_pages.description: Readable sheets that nonetheless paste part of the drawing in as an image. A code-analysis table pasted that way is pixels, and needs OCR.
region_pages.title: Region Pages

SourceProfile.title: SourceProfile

Summary.description:
Counts and provenance for a finished review.

The findings themselves are deliberately not carried here: a Firestore
document is capped at 1 MiB and a large set's finding bodies can approach
it. They live in `findings.json` in the bucket and are fetched from the
signed URL.

conflicts.description: Findings where the declaration and the drawings disagree.
conflicts.title: Conflicts

Summary.title: Summary

info.description: Upload a vector permit set, choose the review parameters, download a marked-up PDF and a findings register. No model calls in the request path.
info.summary: Deterministic Florida Building Code plan review.
info.title: FBC Code Review

get.description: A review is worth keeping: the findings register is the deliverable, and re-running a 24-sheet set to look at it again is thirty seconds and a second copy of the same PDF. The marked-up set and findings.json already live in Cloud Storage, so this lists what is there rather than storing anything new. Rows carry no signed URLs — those are minted per row on `GET /api/jobs/{job_id}`, when a row is actually opened.
get.summary: The caller's own past reviews, newest first.
What was declared with a review. For support and for the audit trail.

post.description: Parses a set and returns the declaration answers the drawings themselves state, so the applicant confirms or corrects them rather than transcribing their own drawing. Starts nothing, stores nothing, and makes no model calls — it is the same pure-Python parse the review runs, stopped after the facts are built. The suggestions are advisory: what the applicant submits to `POST /api/review` is what gets declared.
post.summary: Read what a permit set already states about itself.
Accept a permit set and start a review.
